lesson.intro: A preposition tells us [[where]] something is, [[when]] something happens, or the [[direction]] something moves.
points: Place: in, on, under, behind, in front of, beside, between, above, below, near.
Time: [[at]] + clock time (at 7 o'clock), [[on]] + day or date (on Monday, on 31 August), [[in]] + month, year or part of the day (in May, in 2025, in the morning).
Direction: into, onto, out of, across, through, along, towards.
Between is for two things; among is for more than two.
Since + a point in time (since 2020); for + a length of time (for two years).

examples.text: The cat is sleeping [[under]] the table.
Mei Ling sits [[between]] Siti and Raju.

lesson.tip: For time, remember: AT a time, ON a day, IN a month or year.
